subject: SCIENCE
title: Pushes and Pulls
introduction: Milo pushes a toy cart and pulls a drawer toward himself. How can a force change motion or slow an object?

vocabulary.definition: A push or pull that can change an object’s motion.
To move something away from you by pressing it.
To move something closer to you by drawing it toward you.

activities.instruction: Watch Milo compare pushes, pulls, friction, and their effects.
activities.content: A force is a push or pull; changes in motion depend on combined forces and constraints.

feedback.retry: Check the direction of the push or pull, then ask whether motion starts, changes, or slows.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Text alternative: A force is a push or pull; changes in motion depend on combined forces and constraints.

items.prompt: Milo pushes a cart, pulls a drawer, and watches a ball slow. Which statement about forces is true?

options.text: A force is a push or pull; its effect depends on the other forces and constraints.

items.explanation: A force is a push or pull, but an object may not move if other forces or constraints oppose it. Friction, weight, and surfaces can change the result.

items.prompt: Maxine opens a drawer by moving it toward her. Which example shows a push?

options.text: Let a ball roll without touching it

items.explanation: Pushing sends the toy cart away from Maxine. Pulling brings the drawer closer; a rolling ball and shadow are not examples of the push described.

items.prompt: Milo reads four force claims. Which statement is NOT true?

options.text: Friction can slow a rolling ball

items.explanation: A force does not always make an object move; a heavy box can stay still when pushed. Pulls, pushes, and friction can still have the effects named.

items.prompt: A drawer moves toward Maxine when she opens it. What force is she mainly using?
items.explanation: Maxine pulls the drawer because she brings it closer to herself. Sound, color, and light do not describe the force direction.

items.prompt: Milo rolls a ball across a rug and it slows down. Which statement explains what happened?

options.text: A push always makes things fly
Motion never changes on a rug

items.explanation: Friction rubs against the rolling ball and reduces its motion. A push can start motion, and forces do not always make objects fly or stop instantly.
